title: Rung 1 -- coverage of one triangle against Cycles, no light model in the comparison

subjects.name: Triangle
subjects.notes: No NORMAL accessor. Coverage is decided from Cycles' alpha on the oracle side and from depth != far on ours, so this comparison reads no normal at either end and none is derived: I.26 forbids deriving one and an oracle comparison contains no repair. A rung that compares RADIANCE needs a subject that carries what radiance reads, and that is a different subject.

source.pinReason: first pin; head of main at the time the ladder was written

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: yfov = 2*atan((24/2)/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. roll = -22.5 deg [SET], and the SIGN is a measurement rather than a preference: a camera roll of +r turns the camera's right vector towards its up vector, so the image of the world rotates by -r. At rollRad = -22.5 deg the unit triangle's image bounding box is 1.30656 x 0.92388 units, the HEIGHT binds at k = 704/0.92388 = 762.004109 px/unit and the subject fills 31.5023 % of the frame; at +22.5 deg the box is transposed, the fit drops to 538.818 px/unit and the subject fills 15.7511 %. The three edges then sit at 157.5, 22.5 and 67.5 deg in raster space, every one of them 22.5 deg off the nearest raster axis -- the MAXIMUM of that minimum over all rolls, so this is simultaneously the largest subject and the furthest any edge can be from an axis. Distance 1.9684933221121166 m is what puts 762.004109 px on a unit at 1.3123288814e-3 m/px, aiming at the rotated bounding box centre; a sub-pixel offset of 0.37 px in x and 0.23 px in y is added to the aim so no vertex lies on an exact pixel centre, which leaves the closest vertex 7.77 px inside the frame.
camera.note: The glTF carries no camera, so rung 1's camera is declared here. Superseded 2026-08-12: the first form rolled +12 deg and framed the subject at 19.1144 %, where 31.5023 % was available at the same roll magnitude, the same margin and a strictly better edge-to-axis angle (doc/bugs.md). That the declared camera admits no tie is a geometric predicate over these numbers and the fetched vertices; asserting it is the test's job, not the preparer's.

light.note: Rung 1 compares a coverage mask. The only illumination is Blender's factory world, which costs nothing to match and is left where it is.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: Diffuse BSDF with Roughness pinned to 0, never Principled: Principled at metallic 0 still carries a specular lobe at IOR 1.5 (F0 = 0.04), and it was rewritten in Cycles 4.0. The Diffuse closure at roughness 0 is max(dot(N,w),0)/pi and has not moved.

default.note: The binary mask. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it. This is the recipe the acceptance numbers below are judged on.

coverage.note: The analytic pixel-area fraction: alpha over the full-width box is the coverage, and alpha = 0.5 is the edge through the pixel centre, which gives a signed sub-pixel edge offset instead of a count. Its own per-pixel alpha noise is the instrument floor and is the test's to measure -- it is not asserted here.

notes: The rung rows of doc/requirements.md I.26.5 are being revised, and I.26 rules that this fetched, normal-less subject is the SCHEMA'S WORKED EXAMPLE and never rung 1's final subject. It is what the runner was developed against because it exists and its projection is proven against Blender's analytic answer.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the projected area of the subject's triangles over 1280*720 at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the fetched vertices; exact because the subject is a plane perpendicular to the optical axis, so its perspective image is a similarity
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER: I.26's IoU ~ 1 - P*d/A makes P/A a property of the subject's size, so a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so. The runner recomputes this and refuses a mismatch.
